I understand that there is a single SecurityPolicy schema in Redfish, but in all likelihood, the internal implementation is going to have this content spread across mulitple repositories.  The current properties you are proposing are SPDM-specific and should be hosted by the SPDM daemon, right?  I think we should have a separate SPDM "SecurityPolicy" interface then.  Later on when we add TLS-Policy, that would go elsewhere.

>  The current properties you are proposing are SPDM-specific and should be hosted by the SPDM daemon, right? 

Yes thats correct.

> I think we should have a separate SPDM "SecurityPolicy" interface then.  Later on when we add TLS-Policy, that would go elsewhere.

Done, I have moved this to `yaml/xyz/openbmc_project/Control/Security/SPDM/Policy.interface.yaml` would that work ?

are there any specific D-bus errors returned if SPDMEnabled fails to set?
enabling SPDM communication can be failed for different reasons on the system which can cause failure while setting this property value right

IMO, SPDMEnabled is purely a global policy flag. If its default value is false, switching it to true should simply indicate that SPDM communication is permitted. The system may then initiate SPDM sessions with any already-discovered SPDM capable devices (whether over Network, PCIe, or MCTP).

Because this property only expresses policy and does not perform device communication directly, setting it should not fail. Any operational issues such as connectivity failures, negotiation errors, or device-specific problems would arise later, during actual SPDM exchanges. Those conditions would be surfaced through the individual ComponentIntegrity objects hosted by spdm daemon that represent each SPDM endpoint. So, while SPDM operations may fail for various reasons, those failures should not be reported as errors when setting SPDMEnabled itself.

Are we recommending SPDMEnabled as the trigger for starting spdm device discovery? We need to confirm the system's behavior upon a reboot where SPDMEnabled is already set to true. Does the SPDM daemon (SPDMd) automatically identify and authenticate previously known devices immediately upon device detection/boot completion, or does a manual trigger via Redfish still need to be sent? If manual trigger needed how do we do it?

> Are we recommending SPDMEnabled as the trigger for starting spdm device discovery?

Not really, discovery has nothing to do with this policy. As per the description, this policy dictates/describes whether SPDM communication to SPDM capable devices is enabled/disabled.

> We need to confirm the system's behavior upon a reboot where SPDMEnabled is already set to true. 

Persistency of a policy setting across reboots is not really an interface question - it's an implementation detail, and not relevant for this commit. We can discuss it in the implementation commit when we reach there. 

> Does the SPDM daemon (SPDMd) automatically identify and authenticate previously known devices immediately upon device detection/boot completion, or does a manual trigger via Redfish still need to be sent?

Whether automatic or manual - It totally depends on what the client sets this policy to be.  

> If manual trigger needed how do we do it?

This property is mapped to redfish Security Policy schema. Redfish clients can use that to set the policy. I have already documented the redfish mapping to this interface in my commit message.
Can this be an enumeration then?

Sure, i did give that a try.

Redfish spec allows either `{"ALL"} (all versions)` or `{"NONE"} (no versions)` or `array[string] (which captures specific versions to be allowed)`. So i made this a variant[enum,array[string]] - where the enum captures ALL or NONE & the array captures the specific versions - does this look okay ?
These need to be enumerations.
I tried to apply the same approach as above — let me know if anything looks incorrect.
Why default to disabled for all of these properties?

`SPDMEnabled`: SPDMEnabled is not just a feature toggle. Enabling this changes the trust model of the platform. So IMO, SPDM must be explicitly enabled by the platform owner or provisioning authority(it can be BIOS/TEE or an external verifier like HMC), as initiating SPDM exchanges affects device trust establishment. Hence disabled this by default.

`SPDMSecureSessionEnabled`: Establishing SPDM secure sessions is usually downstream device-dependent and must be explicitly enabled where encrypted device communication is required. In general many SPDM deployments utilize SPDM solely for authentication and measurement retrieval not for secure communication. Hence disabled this by default as well.

`SPDMVerifyCertificate`: In general , certificate validation is performed by an external attestation. The BMC can operate as a conduit for SPDM evidence without acting as the root of trust. So BMC itself acting as a verifier is less typical. Hence made it disabled by default.

`SPDMAllowExtendedAlgorithms`: The requester advertises only the baseline SPDM algorithm set required for interoperability.Extended algorithms may be explicitly enabled to satisfy platform-specific cryptographic or regulatory requirements. Enabling this option expands the negotiated cryptographic surface. Hence made this disabled by default as well.
Can you please elaborate the use case for this policy. If BMC does not want to enable SPDM it can be excluded in the image.

This policy exists so that SPDM behaviour can be controlled via Redfish at runtime. Even if SPDM support is present in the BMC image, a Redfish client can explicitly enable or disable it using the [SecurityPolicy](https://redfish.dmtf.org/schemas/v1/SecurityPolicy.v1_0_3.json) resource.

This avoids the need for multiple BMC images and allows platforms or customers to decide their SPDM posture through configuration, including enabling it later or disabling it for compatibility or security reasons.
When this policy is disabled through redfish expectation in spdmd service is not to perform SPDM discovery and attestation? or we will have the control in BMC to disable spdm service this at run time

> spdmd service is not to perform SPDM discovery and attestation?

The expectation is not do SPDM communication to capable/discovered endpoints.The discovery happens usually at a different layer like mctp/tcp/pcie e.t.c - and this policy does not effect that, so SPDM daemon is free to do any discovery irrespective of this policy setting.

> or we will have the control in BMC to disable spdm service this at run time

No, spdm daemon can be running, it justs sit idle (waiting for discovery events or caches the discovered endpoints and sit idle if this policy is disabled).

None should not be included in the Special SET values for SPDMAllowedVersions, as it does not make sense.
SPDM is present in the image and enabled, but if no versions are supported, it makes SPDM effectively unusable.

But I think that needs to be decided by the admin, Its a patchable property in redfish and the rationale comes from how redfish models *policy intent*, not *operational usability*.

Although setting `SPDMAllowedVersions = NONE` makes SPDM unusable, redfish intentionally allows this because the property expresses administrative security policy, not protocol capability. A patchable policy allows an operator or external policy authority to explicitly state “SPDM must not be used”, even if the feature is present and enabled in the implementation.

This supports valid scenarios such as security lockdowns, vulnerability mitigation, regulatory compliance, or staged provisioning, where SPDM must be temporarily or intentionally disabled without removing the feature itself. 

I think that redfish does not guarantee that a policy configuration results in a usable protocol; it guarantees that *policy intent* can be expressed and enforced deterministically. So including `NONE` as a valid, patchable value is intentional and consistent with other Redfish security policies (for example, TLS cipher policies in the secure policy schema), even if it results in SPDM being effectively disabled.

This is realy tough, where admin needs to take care of so many values
- SPDM should be enabled
- Version should not be none.
- Bunch of these algorithms should not be NONE

This is a one-time PATCH operation. Policies are generally persistent across reboots, so it’s unclear why this would be particularly difficult. If a Redfish client is already verifying the signed SPDM measurements on its own via redfish, then configuring these policies should not be that challenging. If there are concerns about the reasonableness of the defaults, I’m open to discussing them, I don’t believe they should be removed entirely as it gives flexibility.

Redfish says this will be an array of string with potentially a single value of ALL/NONE.  Is it easier on ourselves if we do what you have here or: `array[variant[enum[self.SpecialSetValues], string]]`?  I'm not sure which ends up being easier for us from an implementation stand-point.
I think yours was better , since bmcweb can processes both ALL/NONE or array of versions both the same way. Modified it.

Redfish has this pattern:
```
                    "pattern": "^\\d+\\.\\d+$|^NONE$|^ALL$",
```

Doesn't that mean they are dropping the `update` field in the version?  Why are we using it here?

I did not really pay much attention to the pattern. You are right. 

I defined this as per the SPDM spec numbers per https://www.dmtf.org/dsp/DSP0274. But to me this looks like redfish spec bug. Let me reach out to DMTF for clarity.

I take it back, I think the redfish spec is probably correct. I re-looked at the SPDM spec and it states that `UpdateVersionNumber` : Shall be the version of the specification with editorial updates and errata fixes. Informational; `ignore when checking versions for interoperability.`


The redfish mockup https://redfish.dmtf.org/redfish/mockups/v1/1773 also points to having just the major & minor number alone.
Do we need all these algorithms on Dbus? It should be build time configurations.

I think we should not decide that in code - This is again a patchable property from admins & they get to decide what are the allowed algorithms at the SPDM level, rationale is similar to the response above.
In which scenario None should be set?

IMO, based on the redfish security policy spec, Setting the versions or algorithms to `NONE` is used to explicitly say instances like “SPDM is enabled, but no versions or algorithms are allowed to be used at the moment” This makes the policy unambiguous and prevents SPDM negotiation even if defaults exist or support is added later.
Can you please clarify the same for other allowed and denied properties like Algorithms

Although, the redfish spec is not really clear on the SPDM Policy parameters - they did document some guidance on how we can resolve this type of conflicting requirement from users (Its documented in TLSParameterSet).

Per spec:
```If a value conflicts for the same property between the `Allowed` and `Denied` object, the value of the same property in the `Denied` object shall take precedence.```
Can we drop the "SPDM" prefix on all of these?  Is there some reason for having them?
It just came from my earlier patchsets where I had the TLS policies as well in the same Interface. We can drop it now since we now have a separate one for SPDM alone.
